currentUserGoal: Keep pushing the redesign toward a playable loop by turning the first automation branch into real new-canon gameplay.
changesMade: Added Tiny Sprinkler as a real permanent Memory node instead of a locked placeholder.
Added run-spine automation state with run-owned tinySprinklers count that resets between runs while the permanent Tiny Sprinkler license persists.
Added buyTinySprinkler with license, phase, and Run Touch cost checks. Current run cost is 16 RT.

Added applyTinySprinklerPulse. Each pulse heals 2 HP per run-owned sprinkler, awards Run Touches only from effective missing-HP healing, contributes to dormancy payout only through effective healing, and can clear one targeted wound.

Updated the meta skill tree layout to show Soft Touch and Deeper Roots on the top row, Tiny Sprinkler on the bottom-left branch node, and Scourge Sense as the remaining locked bottom-right placeholder.
Added a Tiny Sprinkler run-tool button that appears only after the permanent license is owned.

Added automatic sprinkler pulses in the prototype scene, with wounded-root priority, small water/halo feedback, and browser debug fields for tinySprinklers, lastTinySprinklerPulseAt, and lastTinySprinklerRootId.
Exposed Tiny Sprinkler through the DOM agent layer as redesign-memory-tinySprinkler and redesign-tiny-sprinkler-button, plus readable Tiny Sprinklers state.
Updated CORE_MECHANICS_REDESIGN.md and CORE_MECHANICS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md to describe the implemented automation slice.
verification: npm run check passed after the Tiny Sprinkler changes: ESLint passed, Vitest passed with 2 files and 26 tests, TypeScript compiled, and Vite built successfully.

New RunSpineSystem unit tests cover missing license, insufficient Run Touches, successful run purchase, run-only sprinkler count reset, persistent license carryover, pulse healing/RT payout, wound clearing, and no full-HP reward minting.

Browser smoke on http://127.0.0.1:5173/?redesign&resetMemory&skipIntro&fastDormancy&sprinklerSmoke=... played a fast run through DOM root buttons, earned enough GT, reached dormancy, and bought redesign-memory-tinySprinkler.
Browser smoke confirmed Tiny Sprinkler purchase reduced permanent GT, persisted permanentUpgrades: [tinySprinkler], and Begin Next Run returned to active play.
Browser smoke earned RT in the licensed run, clicked redesign-tiny-sprinkler-button, confirmed tinySprinklers became 1, lastRunToolKind became tinySprinkler, and runTouches dropped by the 16 RT cost.

Browser smoke waited for an automated pulse and confirmed lastTinySprinklerPulseAt > 0, lastTinySprinklerRootId was set, runTouches and totalRunTouchesEarned increased from effective healing, lastHealingFeedbackKind became sprinkler, readable state mentioned Tiny Sprinklers: 1, and warn/error logs were empty.

knownIssues: Tiny Sprinkler is intentionally first-pass automation: no upgrade scaling beyond buying multiple run units, no dedicated sprite/icon yet, and only small pulse feedback.
Tiny Sprinkler is bought directly as a run tool after the permanent license; there is no separate run shop screen yet.
The options DOM music-on button remains hidden by design; agents unmute by setting redesign-music-volume-range above zero.
The old game still exists on the default route and obsolete stress routes; use ?redesign for the new mechanics work.
nextRecommendedSteps: Manual-test whether Tiny Sprinkler feels understandable, visible, and worth 24 GT plus 16 RT.
Add a small sprinkler icon or in-field object so the automation has a stronger visual identity.
Tune Tiny Sprinkler pulse interval, heal amount, GT cost, and RT cost after playtesting.
Consider adding a compact run-shop strip or tool tray if more run tools are added.
Move next into Scourge Sense or a clearer first-loop goal/reward pass depending on playtest feel.
doNotRevert: Do not bring back old automation systems wholesale; Tiny Sprinkler is a new-canon run-spine automation adapter.
Do not make sprinkler overheal mint RT or permanent GT.
Do not remove the DOM controls for Tiny Sprinkler; they are part of the agent-accessibility contract.
Do not use the obsolete ?stress route as evidence of redesign progress.
